question: At a posted or 85th-percentile speed of 60 mph, what advance placement distance does Table 2C-3 show for deceleration to an advisory speed of 30 mph?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a posted or 85th-percentile speed of 60 mph, Table 2C-3 shows an advance placement distance of 275 feet for Condition B deceleration to a listed advisory speed of 30 mph. This value is a guideline that should be applied with engineering judgment, not a mandatory dimension. Guidance (recommended): - Table 2C-3, 60 mph row, Condition B (deceleration to listed advisory speed): "60 mph 1,100 ft 570 ft 350 ft 325 ft 275 ft 200 ft 100 ft6" — the fourth Condition B column (30 mph advisory speed) is 275 ft. - Per the table's footnote 1, "For Conditions A and B, warning signs with less than 6-inch legend or more than four words, a minimum of 100 feet should be added to the advance placement distance to provide adequate legibility of the warning sign." - Warning sign placement should provide adequate PRT, and "The effectiveness of the placement of warning signs should be periodically evaluated under both day and night conditions." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2C-3 shows, in the 60 mph row under Condition B's 30-mph advisory speed column, a distance of 275 ft. - [Image 3] The full page view of Section 2C.04 includes Table 2C-3 confirming the 60 mph / 30 mph Condition B value of 275 ft. Citations: - Table 2C-3 (p.152) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §804 (p.153) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §5 (p.152) - Page 193
